newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH IN SIGHT OF WEMBLEY - AND RELEGATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MIDDLESBROUGH IN SIGHT OF WEMBLEY - AND RELEGATION.

text.p: Middlesbrough continued their two-pronged assault on a previously untouchable Wembley on Saturday -- but instead of preparing for a celebration they are in danger of ending the season with a wake.
The well-deserved 2-0 victory over at Derby on Saturday put Middlesbrough into the F.A. Cup semifinals for the first time in the club's 121-year history.
And on Wednesday they play the home second leg of their League Cup semifinal against second division Stockport with the cushion of a 2-0 lead.
But while the fans can start thinking about reaching their first major final, possibly soon to be followed by their second, the spectre of relegation looms large.
Middlesbrough are bottom of the premier league, three points adrift of the next club West Ham and five points from safety.

Their cause has not been helped by having three points deducted by the premier league for unilaterally calling off a match against Blackburn when they claimed they were unable to raise a team because of illness and injury.
The club have appealed against the decision but appear unlikely to have it overturned.
It all makes for an unusual situation for manager Bryan Robson, who is doing his best to come to terms with a bizarre season.
"It's very difficult to explain the difference between our cup and league form," the former Manchester United and England midfielder said on Saturday.
"The lads have been very professional in their defensive duties in the cup games. Now we have to get down to serious business in the league."
Defence certainly seems Robson's problem as few teams in the league can match the quality of his multi-national strike force.
Brazilian Juninho, Italian Fabrizio Ravanelli, Dane Mickel Beck and home-grown Craig Hignett can tear opposition defences apart. But they haven't done so often enough this season.
"When the game opens up our four front men are excellent with their movement and the range of their passing," said Robson. "They've done wonders for us in the cups."

Saturday's win followed a 6-1 league victory on Wednesday, also at the expense of Derby. Robson is hoping the confidence gained from that win, and in evidence on Saturday, will stay with his players during the end of season battles ahead.
"Wednesday gave us the confidence to come here and go for the win. We weren't looking for a draw today," said Robson.
"We played very well in the first half but I was particularly pleased with the second half when we had to be very resolute in defence.
Robson is well aware that relegation would be a financial disaster for Middlesbrough and would almost certainly lead to some of his big-name signings leaving the club.
Despite protestations to the contrary, it is hard to see Ravanelli and Juninho playing a pre-World Cup season in the first division.
"Of course, I'd love to win both cups and stay up as well," said Robson when asked yet again which is most important.
History is on Middlesbrough's side if they go all the way in the F.A. Cup.

No club has been relegated after winning the cup, although three runners-up have gone down. Brighton in 1983, Leicester in 1969 and Manchester City in 1926 all ended their seasons with double disappointment.
The League Cup doesn't have quite such a charmed life, however. Norwich went down after winning it in 1985, beating fellow relegation victims Sunderland in the final.
